Lessons.Title: Fossils and Flags
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: independently formulate a bivariate statistical investigation, collect trustworthy paired numerical observations or identify the limits of a simulated dataset, create an appropriate scatter plot, fit and interpret a linear model, examine residuals and correlation, and assess whether any causal claim is justified. Independently authored first-party Edulytiks adaptation of the optional research activity Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 3 Lesson 10, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/3/10/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The original teacher/student project invites authentic data about fossil measurements and flags; our examples are not publisher artifacts or measured specimens.

Original hypothetical flag-design dimensions (width centimetres, height centimetres) are (10,6),(15,9),(20,12),(25,15). All lie exactly on h=0.6w, so a scatter plot shows perfect positive linear association and the constant height-to-width ratio is 3/5. These are *constructed* first-party numerical examples, not measurements of countries' official flags.

Original separate hypothetical fossil illustration: measured-looking numbers (bone length cm, reconstructed model length cm) are (2,8),(3,11),(4,14),(5,18), where hand model y=3x+2 predicts 8,11,14,17 and leaves one residual +1. Nothing in the hypothetical pairs has scientific calibration, so no actual organism size, extinction date or biological conclusion should be inferred. A real fossil dataset needs an identified source, measurement definition, uncertainty and permissions.

Research task: select the flag or fossil theme, identify genuine and legally usable data and their provenance, collect at least several authentic paired numerical observations, show labelled scatter plot, choose a justified fit, describe residuals and r, and state what conclusions follow. If authentic measurements cannot be gathered, submit a simulated mathematics analysis clearly marked as not completing the original research/collection requirement.

Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each (maximum 8): valid research question and source/provenance; transparent genuine observations or simulated limitation; accurate scatter/line/residual/correlation analysis with units; and defensible interpretation identifying selection bias and avoiding causal overclaims. Never grant synthetic fieldwork credit.

KeyConcepts.Title: Paired-data provenance
KeyConcepts.Definition: A research plot needs a traceable measurement definition and source for each paired observation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Distinguish measured data from a constructed classroom demonstration.
KeyConcepts.Example: Flag dimensions (10,6) etc are explicitly fictional designs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Proportional scatter trend
KeyConcepts.Definition: A line through origin can represent fixed width-to-height ratio.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check ratios across every observed pair.
KeyConcepts.Example: For widths 10,15,20,25 and heights 6,9,12,15, each h/w=0.6.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual with scientific limits
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fitted line may approximate records but does not create real scientific evidence.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Calculate residuals and disclose the lack of empirical calibration.
KeyConcepts.Example: For constructed fossil-like (5,18), model y=3x+2 predicts17, residual+1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check constructed flag proportions
WorkedExamples.Question: For widths 10,15,20,25 cm and heights 6,9,12,15 cm, test the ratio.
WorkedExamples.Method: Compute from the exact paired data, verify model assumptions and state what the evidence does not prove.
Steps: All ratios match, giving model h=0.6w.
All points lie on an increasing line through origin; Pearson r=+1 with nonzero variances.
WorkedExamples.Check: All four original paired examples satisfy the model exactly.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compute residuals for the constructed fossil-like values
WorkedExamples.Question: Model y=3x+2 on (2,8),(3,11),(4,14),(5,18).
WorkedExamples.Method: Compute from the exact paired data, verify model assumptions and state what the evidence does not prove.
Steps: A positive residual indicates one point above the trial line.
WorkedExamples.Check: The numbers are invented and have no independent scientific validation.

WorkedExamples.Title: Separate a proposed investigation from performed research
WorkedExamples.Question: What proof is needed before saying an actual museum fossil sample was analyzed?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compute from the exact paired data, verify model assumptions and state what the evidence does not prove.
Steps: Identify a credible museum or published dataset with definitions and rights.
Record real specimen measurements and units, including uncertainties.
Use the actual pairs for a scatter plot and justified statistical model.
Preserve raw values and distinguish model predictions from direct observations.
Without source or measurements, describe the exercise as hypothetical rather than performed fieldwork.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Actual data source and raw pairs are required; the constructed example is not completed empirical research.
WorkedExamples.Check: No original source/provenance or specimen observation was fabricated.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Describing invented flag dimensions as measurements of real nations
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The ratios were chosen to illustrate a model.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label figures as hypothetical design examples.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a model to assert biologically valid fossil reconstruction
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: There is no calibration or provenance for the constructed fossil-like pairs.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require verified empirical source before scientific claims.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Declaring student research completed solely from a worked example
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Task requires genuine data gathering and defense.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Apply teacher rubric and mark missing research explicitly.

SummaryPoints: An independent project must identify actual paired-data provenance and explain what is measured.
Constructed flag data show perfect proportionality but do not describe real national flags.
Constructed fossil-like data illustrate residual calculation without scientific inference.
Teacher reviews original research, data rights and mathematical interpretation; no simulated fieldwork credit.

Visuals.Title: Accessible original bivariate research illustration
Visuals.Description: Fictional numerical points with explicit provenance and limitations; no publisher or real participant data.
